source_text: This module covers how client data and personal data are handled day to day.
Client data is any information a client gives us or that we hold on their behalf.
Personal data is any information that identifies a living individual.
The same file can contain both, and then the stricter rule applies.
Store client data only in approved systems: SharePoint, the client portal, or the case system.
Never move client data to personal email, personal cloud storage, or a messaging app.
A screenshot pasted into Teams is still client data leaving its approved system.
DLP will block some of these transfers, but DLP is a safety net, not a policy.
Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all systems that hold client data.
When you no longer need a local copy, delete it rather than archiving it quietly.
Record retention schedules tell you how long each record class is kept.
Deleting a record early is as serious as keeping it too long.
Unauthorised access means opening a record you have no business reason to open.
Curiosity about a colleague's file is unauthorised access, even with no further action.
A data breach is any loss of control over client or personal data, including a mis-sent email.
A mis-sent email is reportable even if you recall it successfully.
Report any suspected phishing email to the security team within 24 hours.
Working from home does not lower the standard; a shared home printer is not approved storage.
Violations may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination.
If a client asks you to send data by an unapproved route, say no and offer the portal.
